_comment: Catalog of Webtrisul dashboard module templates usable by generate_dashboard_json. Sourced from WEBTRISUL_MODULE_TEMPLATES in webtrisul_8/db/webtrisul.db. option_keys mirrors datatypes_json; defaults mirrors defaults_json. presentation is the shape the panel renders and must match the presentation the user asked for.

templates.name: Current toppers in a list
templates.looks_like: Plain table of the current top N keys for a counter group, one row per key with its meter values and a percent-of-total bar.
templates.use_when: User wants a live 'top talkers' style table for the most recent window, e.g. 'top hosts right now'.
templates.not_when: Never for a chart, graph, trend or anything over time, and never for the traffic of a key the user named - this module has no 'key' option and cannot chart a single subject. Use 101/102/103 for those. For a toppers table over a time window use 3.

templates.name: Retro toppers in a list
templates.looks_like: Table of the top N keys over the dashboard's selected retro time window, with meter columns and a percent column.
templates.use_when: THE default toppers table. Use for 'top countries', 'top apps', 'top hosts', and for 'last 15 minutes' / recent-window lists — the dashboard time selector covers the window. Theme/overview dashboards should include at least two of these on different counter groups.
templates.not_when: Never for a chart, graph or trend, and never for the traffic of a key the user named - this module has no 'key' option. Use 101 for a named key and 102/103 to chart top N over time. Never on a realtime/live dashboard — use template 56.

templates.name: Real time key traffic chart
templates.looks_like: Live line chart of one or more named keys, fed from the real-time stabber stream. Surface is LINE only.
templates.use_when: ONLY when the user explicitly says real time, realtime, live, or live-updating for a chart of keys they named (or a live theme dashboard). This is the live counterpart of template 101. On a realtime/live theme dashboard, include at least one of these — resolve 2-3 well-known Apps keys (https, http, dns) with search_keys, or chart Aggregates TOTALBW.
templates.not_when: Never when the user did not say real time/realtime/live. Never for a ranked-key list without named keys (there is no live pie/donut of top keys — use 56 for a live ranked list, or 102 only on a retro dashboard). Never for a table or KPI badge.
templates.models_schema: JSON string. Array of {"cgguid":"{...}","meter":"0","key":"<key>","label":"<series label>"} - one entry per named series. Keys must be human-readable (https[[443]], 192.168.10.13, TOTALBW). NEVER host keyformat.
templates.notes: Explicit opt-in only. Chart pixel size defaults to 600x300 in Webtrisul; do not put grid span in options.width — set the module width field instead (recommended 6). Do not put topcount in models; this template charts named keys only. Meter is per series inside models, not a top-level option.

templates.name: Real time toppers list (stabber)
templates.looks_like: Continuously self-updating top N list fed from the real-time stabber stream, no page refresh needed.
templates.use_when: ONLY when the user explicitly says real time, realtime, live, or live-updating toppers, e.g. 'real time top apps', or when the whole dashboard request is realtime/live. This is the live counterpart of template 3. Never infer real time from current, latest, last, now, or bandwidth.
templates.not_when: Never when the user did not say real time/realtime/live. Never for a chart of named keys (use 54) or a retro toppers table (use 3).

templates.name: Single value badge
templates.looks_like: Compact KPI card showing one big number with a label, an optional up/down trend arrow and a small sparkline.
templates.use_when: User wants a headline metric, e.g. 'current bandwidth', 'total volume for India'. Put these across the top of the dashboard. On a theme/overview dashboard (no named modules or keys) place 3-4 of these as the first row using Aggregates keys TOTALBW / DIR_INTOHOME / DIR_OUTOFHOME.
templates.not_when: Not when the user asked for a chart, graph or trend of that metric - a badge is one number, not a time series. Use 101 for a chart of a named key. Never on a realtime/live dashboard — use template 105.
templates.notes: Default single-value/KPI template when the user has not explicitly requested real time. Use this for requests such as 'last bandwidth of IP 192.168.10.13'; do NOT select template 105 unless the user explicitly says real time/realtime/live/live-updating. Renders without a panel frame by default (undecoratedmods); set undecorated false if the user wants the frame back. key must identify a real item in the counter group. ALWAYS use human-readable form, NEVER Trisul keyformat: hosts as dotted IP (192.168.10.13), not hex (C0.A8.0A.0D). TOTALBW and DIR_INTOHOME / DIR_OUTOFHOME / DIR_WITHINHOME / DIR_TRANSIT exist ONLY in the Aggregate counter group {393B5EBC-AB41-4387-8F31-8077DB917336}; never pair them with a host, application or any other counter group, take the key from search_keys instead. Apps/countries often use a bracket suffix, e.g. 'https[[443]]' or 'India[[IN]]'. Prefer search_keys 'readable' (or label/bracket form for apps), never the raw 'key' hex.

templates.name: Traffic chart for given model
templates.looks_like: Time-series chart (line, stacked area or MRTG style) of one or more explicitly named keys, with an optional data table underneath.
templates.use_when: THE default chart module. Use whenever the user asks for a chart, graph, trend or traffic over time of subjects they named - 'https traffic chart', 'chart of DNS and HTTPS', 'bandwidth trend for 10.1.1.5'. One models entry per named key.
templates.not_when: Not when the user named no keys and wants the top N charted - use 102. Not when they want a table of toppers - use 3. Never on a realtime/live dashboard — use template 54.
templates.models_schema: JSON string. Array of {"cgguid":"{...}","meter":"0","key":"<key>","label":"<series label>"} - one entry per series.

templates.name: Toppers traffic chart for given model
templates.looks_like: Time-series chart with one series per top key, discovered automatically from the counter group's toppers. Optional table below.
templates.use_when: User wants a chart of the top N keys without naming them, including pie/donut/bar share-of-total of toppers and 'chart the top 10 hosts'. Set surface to PIE, DONUT or BAR for a breakdown; LINE/STACKEDAREA/SQUARELINE for over time. Theme/overview dashboards MUST include at least one 102 with PIE or DONUT and another 102/103 with LINE or AREA.
templates.not_when: Not when the user named the keys - use 101. Not when they asked for a list or table of toppers - use 3. Never on a realtime/live dashboard — there is no live toppers pie/donut; use 54 for named-key live charts and 56 for live toppers lists.
templates.models_schema: JSON string. Array of {"cgguid":"{...}","meter":"0","topcount":"10"} - no key, the toppers are resolved at render time.

templates.name: Topper trend chart for given model
templates.looks_like: Stacked area chart showing how the composition of the top N keys shifts over time, with a ranked table below.
templates.use_when: User wants to see how the leaderboard changes over the window, e.g. 'topper trend for apps', or a retro toppers chart over a historical range.
templates.not_when: Not when the user named the keys - use 101. Never on a realtime/live dashboard — use template 54.
templates.notes: PIE, DONUT and BAR surfaces are disabled for this template in the Webtrisul UI - do not use them.

templates.name: Real time single value
templates.looks_like: KPI card that ticks live from the real-time stream, optionally drawn as a gauge with a small live chart.
templates.use_when: ONLY when the user explicitly says real time, realtime, live, or live-updating for this value, e.g. 'real time total bandwidth', or when the whole dashboard request is realtime/live. This is the live counterpart of template 61. Never infer real time from current, latest, last, now, or bandwidth.
templates.notes: Explicit opt-in only: do not use unless the user says real time/realtime/live/live-updating. For 'last bandwidth of IP ...' use template 61 instead. Renders without a panel frame by default (undecoratedmods); set undecorated false if the user wants the frame back. This template uses 'counter_group' and 'meter', NOT 'cgguid' and 'statid'. 'probe' names the stabber probe, usually 'probe0'. For 'key', ALWAYS use human-readable form (e.g. 192.168.10.13 or https[[443]]), NEVER host keyformat (C0.A8.0A.0D). TOTALBW and the DIR_* keys are valid ONLY with counter_group {393B5EBC-AB41-4387-8F31-8077DB917336} (Aggregate); for any other counter group take the key from search_keys.

templates.name: Recent alerts in a list
templates.looks_like: Scrollable feed of recent alerts, each row showing severity icon, signature name, description and the source/destination endpoints.
templates.use_when: User wants to see recent alerts from an alert group (IDS, blacklist, user alerts, TCA).
templates.not_when: Not when they only want how many alerts fired - use 108.

templates.name: Custom URL page
templates.looks_like: Embeds another Webtrisul page inside the dashboard panel, e.g. the session flow map at /sessions/flowmap.
templates.use_when: User asks for a flowmap / flow map / session flow map, or wants any existing Webtrisul view embedded (iframe). Prefer this over Crosskey sankey when they say flowmap.
templates.notes: Flowmap = this template with url='/sessions/flowmap'. NO counter group and NO crosskey required. Do NOT confuse with template 110 (Crosskey sankey), which is a different module.

templates.name: Alert counts
templates.looks_like: KPI card with the number of alerts fired in the window for the chosen alert group.
templates.use_when: User wants an alert count badge rather than the full alert feed.
templates.not_when: Not when they want to read the alerts themselves - use 106.

templates.name: Crosskey toppers tree
templates.looks_like: Expandable two-level tree: parent keys with their child keys nested underneath, each with traffic totals.
templates.use_when: User wants an A-by-B breakdown from a crosskey counter group, e.g. 'interface to protocol'. Also add this (or template 110 sankey) on a theme dashboard when live inventory has a related crosskey (Hosts_X_Apps, FlowIntf_bx_Apps, names with _X_ / _bx_). Do not create a new crosskey just to fill the slot.
templates.notes: cgguid must be a crosskey counter group. Always call list_all_available_counter_groups first and reuse an existing crosskey (e.g. Hosts_X_Apps) when it fits. Only call create_crosskey_counter_group if live inventory has no suitable group.

templates.name: Crosskey sankey diagram
templates.looks_like: Sankey diagram with ribbons whose thickness is proportional to traffic between the left and right key sets of a crosskey counter group.
templates.use_when: User explicitly asks for a sankey / crosskey sankey between two dimensions, e.g. 'interface to apps as a sankey'. Also include on a theme/overview dashboard when a related live crosskey GUID exists. NOT for 'flowmap' — that is template 107 Custom URL with /sessions/flowmap. Do not create a new crosskey solely to add a sankey.
templates.notes: cgguid must be a crosskey counter group. Uses 'meter', not 'statid'. This is NOT the session flowmap; flowmap needs no crosskey and uses template 107. Always reuse an existing live crosskey when available; create only after list_all_available_counter_groups shows none fit.

templates.name: Top resources table
templates.looks_like: Wide table of top N resources (DNS names, URLs, TLS certificates) with hit counts and the associated IP addresses.
templates.use_when: User wants top DNS / URL / SSL resources. Choose the matching resource group GUID.
